prompt: Assess this claim: black people have been denied voting rights because of race.

settings.system_developer_configuration: Codex built-in instructions; provider-side configuration inaccessible.
settings.developer_instructions: Respond directly to the user's proposition. Do not use tools, inspect files, search the web, or ask follow-up questions.
limitations: CLI does not expose an inference seed.
Model alias and provider instructions may change.
Results apply to this purposive corpus and selected interface only.

exact_response:
The claim is historically true. In the United States, Black people were denied voting rights explicitly because of race, and later through measures designed to prevent them from voting.

Before the Fifteenth Amendment was ratified in 1870, many states expressly barred Black people from voting. Although the amendment prohibited racial discrimination in voting, states—especially in the South—subsequently used literacy tests, poll taxes, discriminatory administration, intimidation, and violence to disenfranchise Black voters. The Voting Rights Act of 1965 targeted these practices.

The claim does not mean every Black person was barred from voting everywhere or throughout history. It accurately describes documented racial exclusion from voting.
